newsitem.title: USA: GOLF - LOGJAM AT THE TOP AS MONTGOMERIE SLIPS BACK TO PACK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - LOGJAM AT THE TOP AS MONTGOMERIE SLIPS BACK TO PACK.

text.p: Straight-shooting Colin Montgomerie went astray Friday as two errant tee shots led to a pair of bogeys that dropped him into a three-way tie for the lead during the second round of the U.S. Open.

Montgomerie, who tamed the sprawling Congressional Country Club course with a five-under 65 for the first-round lead, bogeyed the par-3 second hole and par-4 eighth to slide back to three under par, and a tie with Hal Sutton and Tom Lehman.
Other serious contenders were also crowding closer to the lead in a round that was suspended in the middle of the day for more than two hours because of the threat of lightning.
Ernie Els, the 1994 Open champion, stood at two-under after shooting 67, while Tiger Woods joined the chase with a 67 of his own, launched by a blistering 31 on the front side.
Woods, who floundered at the finish Thursday in posting a 74, stood at one-over-par 141.
Joining Els at two-under was Mark McNulty of Zimbabwe, who began the day at three-under but bogeyed the third hole.

Sutton, who began the day four under par, also bogeyed the 235-yard second hole as had Montgomerie. He stood at three-under with only three holes of his round completed because of the lightning delay.
British Open champion Lehman overcame a bad start to shoot an even-par 70 and was in the clubhouse with a 137 total.
"I got off to a very slow start," said Lehman, who made it unanimous by also bogeying the troublesome second and taking bogey again at the third hole.
"But after that I played very well."
Lehman, perhaps inspired by a birdie binge by playing partner Woods, caught fire with his irons after taking the back-to-back bogeys.

He hit a 9-iron at the fifth hole to less than a foot to birdie the 407-yard par-4, sank a seven-foot birdie putt at the eighth and floated another 9-iron to within two feet for birdie at the par-5 ninth to reach four-under at that point.
Perhaps rusty after sitting out the delay, he bogeyed the par-3 18th by chipping eight feet past the cup after an errant tee shot.

Woods also faltered at the end, coming back from the delay to three-putt the 480-yard 17th for bogey. Woods, who went six over par on the last eight holes of his round on Thursday, nearly landed in the water on the 18th for a second day in a row, but his ball stayed up on the bank and he made par.
Despite his wobbly finish, Woods was pleased.
"The key is to keep getting better every day and you'll be there at the end," the Masters champion said. "I'm back in the tournament.
"The only thing I'm concerned about is to get myself under par and into contention on Sunday."
Scoring in general seemed a little easier during the early going as some light morning rain and a brief but heavy shower during the delay softened the course.
"It's very soft out there, the greens and the fairways," said Lehman. "The course is still in great shape and the greens are holding up. I expect to see some low scores."

Els, who like Woods fired a 31 on the front side, said he was bothered somewhat by the slow pace of play, which was aggravated by the sudden departure of playing partner John Daly, who walked off the course after nine holes.
"I like to play fast. I like to walk up to my ball, get the yardage and then hit it. But we couldn't do that most of the back nine," said Els.
Els was left to play in a twosome with Payne Stewart after Daly departed.

Daly, who has returned to competitive golf after a recent eight-week rehabilitation programme for treatment of alcoholism, later issued a statement saying he had withdrawn from the tournament because of mental and physical fatigue.
